title: Compatibility & Fallthrough PRD for Multi‑Modal Hosted Surface
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD defines a minimal set of compatibility contracts and the fallthrough/canary behavior for the hosted API surface across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank lanes. The goal is to allow model variants and runtime changes to be rolled out with predictable, audited fallbacks so customer applications see bounded behavioral and performance deltas. Scope: define compatibility guarantees (input/output surface, structured outputs, function call semantics, tokenization/stop behavior), canary policy (sampling, metrics, automatic rollback triggers), operator tools (compatibility checker, migration hints), and launch gates. Out of scope: new feature-level semantics for function calling or retraining models; deep model architecture changes.
requirements: Compatibility contract document covering: required fields in JSON response for each lane; function-calling verbatim and fallback to terminal message; canonical tokenization and stop-sequence behavior
SDK-level backward compatible response parsing with version header; SDK unit tests for parsing old and new variants
Observability: per-route drift metrics (embedding cosine drift, generation BLEU/ROUGE delta, latency P95/RPS), and nightly regression alerts tied to canonical prompt-set
Canary policy: sampling fraction configurable per-route, minimum sample size, and delay-before-fallback for stateful KV-cache endpoints
Automatic rollback: define thresholds for errors, high-latency, quality regressions (quality regressions derived from eval set), and cost spikes beyond 30% of baseline
non_functional_requirements: Latency P95 must not degrade by more than 20ms on canary samples vs baseline for same load profile
Embedding cosine similarity to baseline >= 0.98 median on canonical eval set
Throughput: canary path must handle 10k qps in synthetic soak test for dedicated capacity tier
Security: any model variant must be certified by security review before being allowed in private deployments
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility contract doc approved by Eng and DX (design): signatures from Eng lead and API owner
End-to-end SDK smoke that runs: create chat request -> function call -> structured response parse success (automated test)
Canary run that demonstrates: 1% sample for 72h with drift metrics within thresholds and no rollback triggers
Observability dashboards present: per-route latency/cost breakdown, per-model regression panel, canary cohort filter
Automated regression tests in CI: embeddings cosine > 0.98, generation acceptance rate >= 95% for grade prompts
Runbook updated with rollback steps, escalation contacts, and postmortem templates
launch_checklist: Finalize compatibility contract doc and attach to release notes
Add metadata header in API responses: X-Model-Variant and X-Compatibility-Version
Instrument drift and canary dashboards with sample UI filters
Create canary config: default 1% sample, min 500 requests/day, alerting thresholds
QA: run integration smoke across SDKs (python/js/Go) and signoff
Set up canary auto-rollback policy in routing layer with clear thresholds and cooldown
Schedule a cross-functional launch review (PM/Eng/SRE/Sec/Design) two business days before cutover
Prepare customer comms: breaking changes, SDK migration notes, and opt-out steps
Tag release in changelog and link PRs and confluence compatibility matrix

notes: This ticket bundles policy, contract, and operational artifacts that allow runtime teams to flip model variants with bounded customer risk. The core idea is minimal contracts plus observable fallbacks rather than attempting to keep perfect behavioral parity. Where perfect parity is impossible, we mandate a documented migration path and SDK helpers to ease customer upgrades.
